approach: Add a nullable expires_at column (Flyway V3) and an expiresAt component to Link. LinkService.create validates expiresAt or ttlSeconds (InvalidExpiryException: 400 invalid-expiry) and stores the expiry. The cache entry CacheEntry.Found carries expiresAt, so resolve compares it with the injected Clock on every hit, whichever level answered, and needs no database read. An expired link is treated like a deleted one: resolve throws LinkNotFoundException (404 link-not-found), so a probe cannot tell an expired code from one that never existed. LinkCache gains putExpiring(code, url, expiresAt, timeLeft); TieredLinkCache caps the Redis TTL at the time left. RedisLinkCache stores E:<epoch millis>:<url>. BF-1: LinkService.delete evicts the code from L1 and L2 after the transaction commits.

alternativesConsidered.option: An EXPIRED status set by a scheduled job
alternativesConsidered.whyNot: Links would keep redirecting until the job runs, and the job adds a moving part; comparing a timestamp on read is exact.

alternativesConsidered.option: Evict on delete before the commit
alternativesConsidered.whyNot: A concurrent redirect could reload the still-active row and re-cache it.

alternativesConsidered.option: Cross-instance L1 invalidation with Redis pub/sub
alternativesConsidered.whyNot: More moving parts than the requirement needs; the 5-minute L1 TTL bounds the staleness. Follow-up.

apiChanges:
paths:
  /api/v1/links:
    post:
      requestBody:
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              properties:
                expiresAt: { type: string, format: date-time, nullable: true, description: 'in the future, at most ten years ahead' }
                ttlSeconds: { type: integer, format: int64, minimum: 1, maximum: 315360000, nullable: true, description: 'instead of expiresAt' }
      responses:
        '400': { description: 'invalid-expiry: both given, or out of range' }
  /api/v1/links/{code}:
    get:
      responses:
        '200': { description: 'LinkResponse gains expiresAt (absent: never expires)' }
  /{code}:
    get:
      responses:
        '404': { description: 'link-not-found: unknown, deleted (at once) or expired' }
schemaChanges: ALTER TABLE link ADD COLUMN expires_at TIMESTAMPTZ;

components.name: V3__link_expiry.sql
components.responsibility: Nullable expires_at; existing links keep NULL (never expire).

components.name: link.Link / CreateLinkRequest / LinkResponse
components.responsibility: expiresAt on the entity and in the API; the two-argument CreateLinkRequest constructor stays.

components.name: link.LinkService
components.responsibility: Validates the expiry (InvalidExpiryException), checks it on resolve, evicts the cache after a delete commits (BF-1).

components.name: cache.CacheEntry.Found / LinkCache / TieredLinkCache / RedisLinkCache
components.responsibility: Entries carry expiresAt; putExpiring caps the Redis TTL at the time left; Redis value E:<millis>:<url>.

components.name: Configuration
components.responsibility: No new configuration properties: the limits (1 s to ten years) are part of the API contract.

risks.risk: Schema migration on the link table
risks.mitigation: Adding a nullable column without a default is a metadata-only change in Postgres 16; no backfill.

risks.risk: A cache level serves an expired link
risks.mitigation: The expiry travels with the cache entry and is checked on every hit; Redis TTL capped at the time left.

risks.risk: Other instances' L1 serves a deleted link
risks.mitigation: Bounded by the 5-minute L1 TTL; documented; pub/sub invalidation is a follow-up.

rolloutPlan: Migration V3 runs on startup (additive, safe for old instances). Deploy the service; old and new instances can share Redis. No flag: links without an expiry behave as before. Rollback: redeploy the previous version; the column stays and is ignored.
